title: The Coronation on Crystal & The Handlers' Trap
inGameDate: Month of the Sun, Period VIII (Year 1 of the Triumvirate)
summary: The Player Character Triumvirate was crowned in Kordava upon the famed floor of polished crystal. General Don Rodrigo de Valenza stationed his elite caballeros around the palace perimeter, pledging martial protection. High Chancellor Marquis Mateo de Sadoria assumed direct custody of all crown ledgers, officially declaring the state treasury bankrupt due to foreign debt obligations to Argos. The young monarchs received formal bows from the assembled Grandees, though Duke Gonzalo de Guarralid made several cutting remarks testing their martial mettle under pundonor. Underground intelligence confirms that republican cells in The Pit view the coronation as a farce, while the outlawed Church of Nemeth has stepped up nocturnal recruitment.
activeThreads: The Empty Vaults: Marquis Mateo has refused royal requests for personal guard stipends.
The Whispering Pit: Republican agitators are circulating pamphlets claiming the Restoration Council murdered the republican founder in Period VI.
The River Embargo: Rumors that Duke Gonzalo's retainers in Jerida are preparing to halt crown timber barges.

title: The Thief's Bargain & The Shadows of the Corn Armada
inGameDate: Month of the Sun, Period VIII (Day 4 of the Triumvirate)
summary: Desperate for independent wealth to bypass High Chancellor Marquis Mateo's bankrupt treasury, the PC Triumvirate slipped in disguise into the Lower Wards of Kordova. In The Drowned Rat, a squalid dive clinging to the sewer outfall of The Pit, they met Joaquin 'El Grajo' Valiente—a starving cutpurse crushed by the city's economic collapse and an 80-sovereign blood-tithe debt to his guildmaster. In exchange for coin and a blood-oath guarantee of being included in any future schemes, Joaquin agreed to introduce the PCs to the elusive Night Guild of Kordova. Joaquin revealed that an all-out underworld war is erupting: a displaced thieves' guild from the southern port of Velasco, violently expelled by the newly arrived religious refugees from Kordova, has invaded the capital to muscle in on local turf. With Kordova's municipal granaries down to four days of food, the Triumvirate took a bold gamble: they dispatched a formal royal herald to invite Capitán-Commodore Nikolos Voros of the offshore Argossean Grain Fleet to the High Alcázar to 'negotiate grain prices.' In secret, the young monarchs are laying plans to steal the entire 50,000-bushel cargo—either by trapping the Commodore on trumped-up criminal charges in court or by orchestrating a midnight boarding operation with cutthroats from the Night Guild or the Velasco Syndicate. Meanwhile, taking advantage of their incognito journey into the city, the player necromancer broke off to visit his old alma mater, the Royal University of Kordava. Found clinging to the western cliffs above The Pit in near-total ruin after the civil wars, the campus is on the verge of eviction by High Chancellor Marquis Mateo. In the Leaning Spire of Printius, the player met his former mentor, Dean Don Baltasar de Argote. Rather than despairing, Dean Argote enthusiastically shared the player's passion for necromancy and expressed unbridled delight at the prospect of taking the university in a new, zombie-focused direction—transforming the battered institution into a state-sponsored College of Applied Thanatology and Deathless Industry, provided the player can secure 500 gold sovereigns in funding. In a tavern dive off the University Quadrangle, the player necromancer also made an unexpected, fateful discovery: Don Tristán de Revella y Montalbán, an aristocratic member of his old college fraternity (La Cofradía del Cuervo Dorado). Sunk into dissolute alcoholism and drowning in debts following the slaughter of his family during the civil war, Tristán is the sole surviving heir to the lost mountain estate of Revella. Seeing an audacious opportunity to solve the Crown's crushing resource crisis, the player hatched a plan to reinstate Tristán to his ancestral seat by royal decree, hoping to offload the headache of seizing and managing Revella's immensely valuable tin mines to his indebted fraternity brother. However, complications abound: Tristán's chronic inebriation makes him a volatile liability; the mines are currently fortified by an entrenched rebel miner commune (La Hermandad del Pico); Duke Gonzalo de Guarralid is massing troops at the highland pass to annex the veins; and while drunk, Tristán unwittingly signed away overlapping deeds to the mines to Argossean factors, the Night Guild, and Chancellor Sadoria's treasury clerks.
activeThreads: The Guild Audition: Joaquin has arranged a midnight descent through the sewer sluices to the Cistern of the Blind Saint to meet Guildmaster Don Beltrán de Soto.
The Velasco Incursion: Displaced maritime cutthroats under Capitán Don Casimiro de Velasco are ambushing Kordovan lookouts and seizing dockside protection rackets.
The Refugee Backlash: News arrives from the south that Kordovan religious refugees in Velasco have completely overthrown the city council, sparking panic among the Grandees.
Joaquin's Debt Clock: Joaquin has 48 hours to pay his 80-sovereign fine to Don Beltrán before the guild breaks his fingers and sells him to Master Vane's corpse carts.

The Grain Fleet Summons: Commodore Nikolos Voros and Factor Demetrio Phokas have accepted the royal invitation to negotiate grain prices at the High Alcázar; the PCs must prepare their legal ambush or finalize night-boarding plans.
The Famine Clock: Kordova has less than 96 hours of grain remaining before devastating bread riots erupt across the Lower Wards and The Pit.

The Dean's Endowment: Dean Don Baltasar de Argote is eager to transform the ruined Royal University of Kordava into a premier necromantic college if the PC Necromancer can secure 500 gold sovereigns in funding before Chancellor Sadoria's eviction bailiffs arrive.

The Revella Tin Gambit: Reinstating the PC Necromancer's dissolute fraternity brother, Don Tristán de Revella, to his ancestral highland estate to seize control of the kingdom's richest tin mines before Chancellor Sadoria's Argossean creditors or High Duke Gonzalo annex the veins.

title: The General's Muster & The Road to the Salt-Gate
inGameDate: Month of the Sun, Period VIII (Day 6 of the Triumvirate)
summary: Stung by ongoing unrest and desperate to enforce martial discipline over the restless borderlands, General Don Rodrigo de Valenza entered the Royal Presence in full battle plate. He delivered grave intelligence: the border settlement of San Severo del Vado—commanding the sole heavy wagon bridge on the southern highway midway between Kordova and the hostile theocratic port of Velasco—has risen in open armed rebellion under La Hermandad de las Espinas. Starving peasants, royal army deserters, and desperate Gnostic religious refugees have barricaded El Puente de los Desamparados, driven out crown bailiffs, and seized the royal granaries. Don Rodrigo announced an immediate punitive expedition of 200 heavy cavalry and infantry to storm the crossing and execute the rebel ringleaders. Refusing to remain cloistered palace puppets under the thumb of High Chancellor Marquis Mateo, the PC Triumvirate made a daring sovereign choice: they ordered their warhorses saddled to personally accompany General Valenza's column. Their goals: present themselves to the kingdom as active, warrior monarchs, learn the realities of the frontier provinces, and scrutinize General Don Rodrigo's tactics, officer corps, and secret motivations up close. As the column marched south across parched scrubland, Rodrigo began testing the young monarchs with ruthless tactical conundrums by the evening campfire, while intelligence hints that the rebel commander is an old ghost from Rodrigo's own blood-soaked past.
pundonorStatus: Maintained (Mounted royal progress; martial bearing recognized by caballeros)
activeThreads: The Executioner's Crown: Rodrigo demands the PCs sign death warrants for Capitán Andrés, Madre Soledad, and Alcalde Cadenas upon reaching San Severo; the PCs must decide whether to execute, pardon, or engineer a covert compromise.
The Deserter's Ledger: Intelligence suggests rebel leader Capitán Andrés de Hojeda possesses sealed proof of Rodrigo's war crimes from Period VII hidden in the village crypts.
The Velasco Relief Clock: A war-cog carrying 80 fanatical holy warrior-monks from Velasco is sailing up the Rio Salado; the PCs have less than 12 hours upon arrival to prevent an all-out holy war.
The Salt & Grain Accord: San Severo controls the gateway to Velascan salt; negotiating a settlement could alleviate Kordova's salt famine without bloodshed.
The Grain Fleet Summons: Commodore Nikolos Voros and Factor Demetrio Phokas remain in Kordova awaiting the delayed royal grain conference.
The Dean's Necromantic Endowment: Dean Argote awaits the 500-sovereign endowment to transform the university into a College of Applied Thanatology.
The Revella Tin Gambit: Don Tristán de Revella awaits royal marching orders to reclaim his ancestral tin mines.
